title: Oval-Pan Snapper with Mild Cajun Pecan Gravy
description: Smoked paprika, thyme and smooth toasted pecan paste give two individual pans of poached snapper a mild Louisiana-style gravy.
equipment: Two small oval cast iron pans with foil or fitted lids

ingredients.name: skinless red snapper fillet
ingredients.note: Weight after skin and pin bones are removed. Divide into two even portions about 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick. Fully thaw before cooking.

ingredients.name: smooth unsalted roasted pecan paste
ingredients.note: Use finely milled pure pecans without pieces. Stir before measuring.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Choose unsalted plain meat-and-water broth without a vegetable blend.

steps.title: Warm the spices
steps.text: Melt {butter} in the HexClad over low heat. Add {paprika}, {thyme} and {garlic} and stir for 20 seconds, just until fragrant.

steps.title: Loosen the pecan paste
steps.text: Whisk {pecan} with a little {broth} until smooth. Whisk it into the skillet with the remaining broth and bring to a gentle simmer.

steps.title: Fill the oval pans
steps.text: Ladle enough thin pecan broth into each small oval cast iron pan to come partway up the fish when added. Keep the remainder in the HexClad.

steps.title: Poach the snapper
steps.text: Divide {fish} between the ovals and spoon liquid over the surface. Cover and maintain a bare simmer on low burners for 4–9 minutes, checking the centers from the side after 4 minutes.

steps.title: Pull each portion
steps.text: Lift each fillet out at 135°F. Place it on a warm plate with a spoonful of the reserved warm pecan broth, cover and rest for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Gather the gravy
steps.text: Pour the remaining liquid from both ovals into the HexClad. Bring the combined gravy to a full boil for 1 minute.

steps.title: Bind the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble gently for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check carryover and doneness
steps.text: After resting, check each thickest center for about 140°F. Open a natural seam with a fork. The center should be opaque and separate easily into flakes. If either cue is unclear or the center is below 140°F, finish covered in hot sauce in the HexClad over low heat to a measured 145°F, checking every minute.

steps.title: Spoon into bowls
steps.text: Set each portion in a shallow bowl. Spoon the glossy pecan gravy under and over the flakes.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/4 cups for two. Make ahead: Mix the paprika, thyme and garlic the day before and refrigerate covered. Stir the pecan paste smooth before cooking. Refrigerate in shallow portions within 2 hours. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the fish submerged in the gravy for up to 1 month. Whisk the gravy after reheating to disperse the nut oil. Fridge reheat: Warm a portion covered in its sauce over medium-low heat in the HexClad. Add a little water if it has thickened in storage. Check from 5 minutes and heat to 165°F at the coldest center. Freezer reheat: If frozen, thaw the covered portion in the refrigerator overnight, then follow the fridge method. Option A uses smoked paprika and garlic. For gentler Option B, use half as much sweet unsmoked paprika and omit the garlic. Avocado oil can replace the butter for a dairy-free dish. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 253 kcal, 31.5 g protein, 5.6 g total carbohydrate, 11.3 g fat, 1.2 g fiber, 116 mg sodium. Includes both the fish and its full share of sauce and any rice or potatoes listed. Sodium varies with the broth.

steps.text: Whisk {pecan} with a little {broth} until smooth. Whisk it into the skillet with the remaining broth and bring to a gentle simmer.

steps.text: Ladle enough of the warm pecan broth into a snug Dutch oven to cover the bottom. Nestle {fish} inside, cover and hold over low heat. Check after 4 minutes and every minute thereafter until 145°F.

steps.title: Hold the fish
steps.text: Lift out the fillets and cover on a warm plate. Pour the cooking liquid back into the HexClad and boil for 1 minute.

steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble gently for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.
